purpose: Inspect-only profile of the 8 entertainment-media source files (books, movies, Netflix, Spotify, top-chart music, video games) used for cross-source TF-IDF + K-Means + LDA analysis.

target_task.cluster_metrics: dominant LDA topic + top-5 words; coherence_score = mean cosine similarity between cluster members and K-Means centroid (subsample 500 with np.random.seed(42) when cluster > 500); up to 5 representative items
target_task.output_schema: cluster_id, dominant_topic, top_topic_words, coherence_score (4dp), representative_items ('source: title' joined by ' | '), 10 rows

notes: CSV is multiline-quoted (raw lines 45572 > parsed rows 45466); always read with on_bad_lines='skip' + low_memory=False.
'genres' and 'production_companies' are stringified python lists of dicts -> require ast.literal_eval to extract 'name'.
Only 538 rows fall in 2017-2020 and the file is popularity-sorted, so the first rows are all pre-2014; strict 2017-2020 filtering would nearly empty this source.
Richer/free-text ('overview' mean ~390 chars/record) -> dominant contributor of English vocabulary.

combined_corpus_plan.unit: one document per item, field set = source_key, title, text
combined_corpus_plan.expected_size: ~160k documents (movies 45,466 + books 11,123 + netflix 8,807 + spotify 114,000 + top2017 100 + top2018 100 + top50_2020 50 + vgsales 16,598) before dedupe/cleaning

text_recipe.movies: title + overview + tagline + genres(names via ast.literal_eval) + production_companies
text_recipe.netflix: title + listed_in + description + cast + director + type
text_recipe.spotify: track_name + artists(';'->' ') + album_name + track_genre (genre token repeated to weight it)

drop_rules: drop documents whose cleaned text is empty or < 2 tokens

risks_and_recommendations: Year coverage is uneven: only Netflix actually centers on 2017-2020 (51%); movies 1.2%, books 0.17%, vgsales 0.02%, and Spotify has no year column. A hard 2017-2020 filter would leave ~4.7k documents (mostly Netflix) and make cross-source clustering meaningless, so the pooled corpus should NOT be hard-filtered by year.

Severe length imbalance across sources (movies ~390, netflix ~316, books ~77, spotify ~60, charts ~30, games ~48 chars). TF-IDF length normalization helps, but short-text sources (Spotify/charts/games) rely on categorical tokens (genre, artist, publisher) to have any signal.
Spotify is 71% of all documents and is stored in genre blocks -> shuffle (random_state) before any 500-item subsample so the coherence subsample is not one genre.
Token hygiene needed: lowercase, strip 'feat.'/punctuation, replace '/' and ';' inside author/artist lists with spaces, remove language codes and numeric-only tokens.
The movies CSV must be parsed with on_bad_lines='skip' and its dict-like 'genres' column parsed with ast.literal_eval.
